task.name: Two paths decide whether a branch's work has landed using different evidence, so a squash-merged branch is preserved forever
task.story_text:
## What

One resolver answers whether a branch's work has landed, and both the worktree sweep and
resume triage consume it instead of each deriving its own answer from different evidence.

## Why

Two code paths ask the same question and disagree, because one uses a proxy that a squash
merge invalidates.

Resume triage resolves `skip_merged` from audit, PR, or issue-commit evidence, and has a
dedicated merged-branch path. It recognises a landed branch.

The worktree sweep asks something narrower — are this branch's commits present on origin?
Its own comment states the intent:

> Absence of commits missing from origin is what establishes the work exists elsewhere, and
> it is also what separates a never-pushed branch from one whose remote ref was deleted
> after merging.

That reasoning holds for a merge commit and fails for a squash. A squash landing produces one
new commit with a different SHA, so the branch's own commits never appear on origin as
commits. The count is permanently non-zero, and the branch is preserved on every run forever.

Observed today, on a sprint that had nothing to do with either branch:

```
⚠ WORKSPACE  preserving worktree feat/issue-2553 — 4 commits not present on origin
⚠ WORKSPACE  preserving worktree feat/issue-2365 — 2 commits not present on origin
```

Both are closed, both landed, and both features are live in the base branch — #2553 squashed
in PR #2577, #2365 squashed in PR #2461, whose feature is present at
`src/theforge/coordinator/issue_cost.py`. Neither branch holds unlanded work. They have
warned on every sprint since they merged and will continue to.

The conservatism is right and should not be weakened: preserving a branch that might hold
unlanded work is the correct default, and a sweep that deletes real work is far worse than
one that keeps stale directories. What is wrong is that the sweep decides on weaker evidence
than the codebase already has, so it cannot distinguish a never-pushed branch from a
squash-merged one and treats both as unsafe.

The accumulation this produces is the symptom recorded in #2653; this issue is the mechanism
behind it, and fixing the resolver is what would let a reaper act.

## Acceptance criteria

- A single resolver reports whether a branch's work has landed, and both the worktree sweep
  and resume triage consume that answer rather than each computing one.
- The resolver reports a branch as landed when its work reached the base branch through a
  squash merge, where the branch's individual commits never appear on origin.
- A branch whose work has not landed is still preserved. Widening recognition of landed work
  never widens deletion of unlanded work.
- A branch the resolver cannot classify is preserved, and the report names which evidence was
  absent, so an operator can separate a genuinely unlanded branch from an undecidable one.
- Non-regression, from branches present today: `feat/issue-2553` (squashed in #2577) and
  `feat/issue-2365` (squashed in #2461) both report as landed. A branch carrying local-only
  commits with no merge evidence reports as unlanded and is preserved.

- The shared resolver keeps every evidence source resume triage distinguishes today — the
  landing audit, git topology, the issue-commit source, the merged-PR lookup, and the guarded
  closing-reference fallback — together with the check that lets recorded audit evidence
  contradict an apparent merge. No branch that resolves to `skip_merged` today resolves to
  anything weaker afterwards.
- The resolver returns a landed / unlanded / undecidable answer carrying which source decided
  it and, where undecidable, which evidence was absent. It does not collapse to a boolean, and
  it does not reduce to the sweep's present question of whether a branch's commits appear on
  origin.
- A branch the resolver reports as landed becomes reclaimable by the sweep. Where such a
  branch is otherwise clean, unlocked and unescalated, its commits being absent from the base
  branch no longer holds it, so `feat/issue-2553` and `feat/issue-2365` stop being preserved
  rather than merely being reported differently.

## Example

Today, every run:

```
⚠ WORKSPACE  preserving worktree feat/issue-2553 — 4 commits not present on origin
⚠ WORKSPACE  preserving worktree feat/issue-2365 — 2 commits not present on origin
```

After, the same two branches:

```
✓ WORKSPACE  feat/issue-2553 landed via squash (PR #2577) — reclaimable
✓ WORKSPACE  feat/issue-2365 landed via squash (PR #2461) — reclaimable
⚠ WORKSPACE  preserving worktree feat/issue-9999 — no merge evidence; 3 local commits
```

The third line is the case the sweep exists for, and it still preserves.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] Gate evidence was unavailable; review found blocking gaps where the sweep and resume triage still make landing decisions outside the shared resolver and topology evidence fails on a real merge. | [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Unified branch landing resolver is correctly implemented and cleanly integrated into worktree sweep and resume triage, fully resolving issue #2795. | [anthropic-claude-haiku-4-5-cli] The shared branch-landing resolver correctly answers "has this branch's work landed?" for both callers (sweep and resume triage), detects squash merges via PR lookup and closing references, preserves all four evidence sources in precedence order, and introduces comprehensive tests covering edge cases including the two regression branches named in the issue. The tri-state (LANDED/UNLANDED/UNDECIDABLE) design distinguishes "work is absent" from "we cannot tell", enabling operator-actionable preservation messages. All acceptance criteria are satisfied.

findings.description: The worktree sweep removed a clean branch whose commits were present on an unrelated origin tracking ref but whose content had not landed on the configured base branch.
A branch merged by a normal merge commit without audit, PR, or closing-reference evidence resolved as undecidable instead of landed.
Resume triage still returned skip_merged from a direct prior-APPROVE audit check after the shared resolver path had produced no landed result.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3's 'only landed is reclaimable' wording can regress existing safe cleanup cases in tests/test_worktree_lifecycle_hygiene.py: empty branches and fast-forward-merged branches without audit evidence are currently removed. The existing src/theforge/sprint/dag.py topology implementation also cannot prove the ordinary real-git ancestor case as written, because after branch is an ancestor of base, base..branch necessarily has zero commits.
  Suggestion: While moving topology into Step 1, explicitly represent the existing safe no-unique-work/origin-containment cases as resolver evidence, or otherwise retain their safe cleanup path without weakening unlanded preservation. Keep the existing empty-branch and real fast-forward sweep tests alongside the new squash tests.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Blast radius on test patch targets. Step 2 rewires external dependency satisfaction (dag.py:736) away from _is_branch_merged, but seven test files outside Step 4's list patch that exact symbol and would silently stop taking effect: tests/test_sprint_github_query.py:517, tests/test_cli_sprint_query.py:234,285, tests/test_story_sources.py:895,910 (patching theforge.sprint.dag._is_branch_merged) and tests/test_coord_logging.py:815, tests/test_coord_resume_cached_already_done.py:68,96,122, tests/test_story_type.py:212, tests/test_sprint_intake_remediation_cost.py:151,235 (patching theforge.coordinator.preflight_flow._is_branch_merged). Step 4's file list names only test_sprint_runner/test_sprint_resume/test_worktree_lifecycle_hygiene/test_coord_preflight_cached. This is the plan's stated Risk 1, only partially retired by the 'narrow compatibility path' mitigation.
  Suggestion: Either keep dag.py:736 and preflight_flow.py:1177,1374 calling the module-local _is_branch_merged wrapper (so existing patch targets stay live), or extend Step 4 to repoint the patch targets in all seven files. State which, so the dev does not discover it via a red suite.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] The sweep has a second preservation gate after the commit-presence one. workspace.py:836 requires merged or branch_gone (git branch --merged origin/<base>, plus refs/remotes/origin/<branch> existence) before _remove_worktree runs. A squash-landed branch is not an ancestor of origin/base, so merged is False; if its remote ref still exists, branch_gone is also False and the worktree is preserved even after the new resolver says landed — the AC would be satisfied only for the subset whose remote ref was deleted. Step 3 only names the commit-presence gate.
  Suggestion: In Step 3, have a landed resolver result short-circuit both gates (treat landed as satisfying the merged/branch_gone condition), and add a Step 4 case where the squash-landed branch's origin ref still exists to prove it is reclaimed rather than silently preserved.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Wiring the resolver into the sweep adds a gh merged-PR lookup and audit read per candidate worktree, inside a loop that previously ran only cheap local git commands, and the sweep runs on every WORKSPACE entry.
  Suggestion: Order the resolver's sources so local evidence (audit, topology) decides before any gh subprocess, and treat a failed gh probe as undecidable rather than blocking — which Risk 2's mitigation already implies.

finding_registry.description: The worktree sweep removed a clean branch whose commits were present on an unrelated origin tracking ref but whose content had not landed on the configured base branch.
A branch merged by a normal merge commit without audit, PR, or closing-reference evidence resolved as undecidable instead of landed.
Resume triage still returned skip_merged from a direct prior-APPROVE audit check after the shared resolver path had produced no landed result.

When GitHub reports a merged PR for a branch whose current content is still absent from the configured base branch, the resolver returns landed before checking the content and the sweep can reclaim that clean worktree.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
